how.title: How credits work
items: Credits are bought in packages; the price per credit drops for bigger packages.
Media & Data server features use your plan's monthly quota; credits are for VR, the Website Builder and extra quota.
Tools that run in your browser (data conversion, developer utilities, some media tools) are always free and never use credits.
Server features show a cost estimate before running. Credits are only deducted after the server reports success; failed or cancelled = free.
Repeated clicks and duplicate requests are sent with an idempotency key, so you're never charged twice.
One-time items (premium templates, presets, elements, website slots) are unlocked once and recorded on your account.
Balance, payments, and access are always verified by the server — never by what the browser shows.

how.title: How plans work
items: Quota is counted per month from your start date, also for yearly plans. Unused quota does not carry over.
Images, PDFs, spreadsheets, GIFs and frames count per run. Upscaling 3×/4× = 2 runs; OCR over 50 pages = 3 runs.
Video compression and audio extraction count per minute of duration.
Quota is only used when processing succeeds. Failed or cancelled = not used.
Out of quota? Add 50 runs or 30 video minutes for 10 credits, valid until the end of that month's period.
Upgrade any time; the remaining value of your old plan becomes a discount. Downgrade after the active plan ends.
Remaining old feature packs (from before subscriptions) are used first, and their owners get 1 month of Basic free.
When the video server is busy, Pro and Team jobs are still processed first.

docs.description: Guides for every OneWebDev tool: how to use it, file formats, and tips.

getting-started.title: Start here
getting-started.summary: OneWebDev is a set of developer tools for converting data, processing media, and building websites. Every tool runs right in your browser, with no account.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.body: The app has four menus in the sidebar: **Data**, **Media**, **Website Builder**, and **VR**, plus **Docs**.
items: **Data** — Excel → JSON, Excel/JSON → SQL, PDF Tools, and Developer Utilities.
**Media** — image & audio conversion, color picking, background removal, upscaling, metadata removal, favicons, and OG images.
**Website Builder** — Page Design, Full Website, Website Templates, and Global Settings.

sections.heading: How to use
items: Pick a tool from the sidebar or from a card on the Dashboard.
Press **Help** in the page header to open a short guide for that tool without leaving the page.
Page addresses start with a language code (`/id/...` or `/en/...`); switch language any time from the header.

sections.heading: Where your data is processed
items: Files are processed on your device and are never sent to a server.
Page designs, website folders, icons, and fonts are stored in this browser's storage, not in an online account.

sections.heading: Capacity
items: **Unlimited** website folders and page designs.
**All** website templates can be previewed, downloaded, and edited.
Every section, element, and 360° Tour feature can be used and exported.

pairs.q: My designs or icons are missing on another device.
pairs.a: Website Builder data is stored per browser. Use the same browser and device, and don't clear site data.

data-excel-json.title: Excel → JSON
data-excel-json.summary: Turn Excel sheets (.xlsx/.xlsm) or CSV/TSV into JSON or a JavaScript module, fully in the browser.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.body: Converts many files at once, lets you pick a sheet per file, then download results one by one or as a ZIP. Files are never sent to a server.

sections.heading: How to use it
items: Drop files on the upload area or click to choose them.
Set **Output options**: JSON or **JS module (.js)**, **First row as column names**, and **Pretty print (indent)**. Option changes apply to all results immediately.
Pick another sheet from the file card's sheet list if needed.
Press **Download** per file or **Download ZIP** for all results.

sections.heading: Input & output formats
items: Input: `.xlsx`, `.xlsm`, `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.txt`.
Output: `.json` (array of objects, or array of arrays when column names are off) or `.js` with `export default data`.
CSV is read as plain text (`007` stays `007`); `,` `;` tab or `|` delimiters are detected automatically; non-UTF-8 text is read as Windows-1252.
Dates become ISO text, formulas use their stored result, duplicate column names get a `_2` suffix.

sections.heading: Limits
items: Max. **20 MB** per file and **30** files at a time.
Legacy `.xls`, `.ods`, `.xlsb`, `.numbers` formats cannot be read in the browser.

pairs.q: A .xls/.ods (legacy) file cannot be read.
pairs.a: Re-save it as .xlsx or .csv, then upload it again.

pairs.q: "This is not a modern Excel (.xlsx) file"
pairs.a: Probably a renamed .xls or a damaged file. Open it in Excel and save as .xlsx.

pairs.q: The Excel file is corrupt or password-protected.
pairs.a: Remove the password protection and save again.

pairs.q: Some files were skipped.
pairs.a: Check the message above the list: unsupported format, over 20 MB, or more than 30 files.

data-sql.title: Excel/JSON → SQL
data-sql.summary: Generate ready-to-run INSERT INTO queries from Excel/CSV or JSON, with column mapping and database dialects, right in the browser.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.body: Turns data rows into `INSERT` statements for MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, or generic (ANSI) SQL. Data is never sent to a server.

sections.heading: How to use it
items: Choose a source: an Excel/CSV file, or JSON (paste text or **Open .json file**).
Fill in **Table name**, then set each column: include/exclude it and rename the database column.
Choose the **INSERT style** (**One INSERT, many rows** or **One INSERT per row**), **SQL dialect**, and **Empty values become NULL**.
The preview shows part of the rows; **Copy all** and the `.sql` download contain all data.

sections.heading: Input & output formats
items: Excel/CSV input is the same as Excel → JSON (`.xlsx`, `.xlsm`, `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.txt`, max. 20 MB).
JSON input: an array of objects (or array of arrays → columns `kolom_1`, `kolom_2`, …); `.json` files max. 10 MB.
Identifiers are quoted per dialect: MySQL with backticks, PostgreSQL `"x"`, SQL Server `[x]`; generic stays unquoted when safe.
Booleans: `TRUE`/`FALSE` for PostgreSQL & generic, `1`/`0` for MySQL & SQL Server. Unicode text on SQL Server uses `N'...'`; MySQL backslashes are escaped.

sections.heading: Limits
items: Column types (Number/Boolean/JSON/Text) are detected from the first 200 non-empty values; mixed values count as Text.
This tool only generates SQL text; it does not connect to your database.

sections.heading: Examples
items: Many-rows mode: `INSERT INTO "products" ("name", "price") VALUES ('Coffee', 18000), ('Tea', 9000);`

pairs.q: "Fill in a table name to build the query."
pairs.a: Type a name in the **Table name** field.

pairs.q: A database column name is empty or used more than once.
pairs.a: Give every included column a unique name (case-insensitive).

pairs.q: Invalid JSON at line X, column Y.
pairs.a: Fix the character at that position, or clean it up first with **JSON Formatter & Validator** in Developer Utilities.

data-utilities.title: Developer Utilities
data-utilities.summary: 18 small tools: JSON, JS Object, CSV, Base64, URL, JWT, hash, timestamp, UUID, regex, text diff, case & slug, dummy text, cron explainer, color contrast, and SVG optimizer. Everything runs in your browser; input never leaves your device.

sections.heading: Tool list
items: **JSON & data**: JSON Formatter & Validator, JSON Minifier, JSON → JS Object, JS Object → JSON, JSON ↔ CSV.
**Encoding & security**: Base64 Encode/Decode, URL Encode/Decode, JWT Decoder, Hash Generator.
**Time & generators**: Timestamp Converter, UUID Generator.
**Text, web & design (v10)**: Regex Tester, Text Diff, Case & Slug Converter, Dummy Text, Cron Explainer, Color Contrast Checker, SVG Optimizer.

sections.heading: How to use it
items: Pick a tool from the **Utilities** list, paste text or **Open file**, then press an action button (e.g. **Format**, **Encode**, **Decode**).
Shortcut: Ctrl/⌘ + Enter to run.
**Use as input** moves the result into the input for the reverse action (e.g. encode then decode).
Results can be copied or downloaded as a file.

sections.heading: Tool details
items: JSON Formatter: 2/4-space or tab indent, **Sort keys (A–Z)**, and line/column error location.
JS Object → JSON only reads literals (strings, numbers, booleans, null, objects, arrays); code is never executed.
JSON ↔ CSV: `,` `;` or tab delimiter; CSV → JSON uses the first row as column names when enabled.
Base64 supports UTF-8 and the URL-safe variant; URL supports `encodeURIComponent`/`encodeURI` and query parsing.
Hash: SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512 (hex or base64) via Web Crypto. Timestamp: s/ms/µs/ns ↔ ISO, UTC, local time. UUID v4: up to 500 at once.

sections.heading: Limits
items: No upload: everything runs in the browser.
**JWT Decoder only decodes** the header & payload and shows `exp`/`iat`/`nbf`. The signature is **NOT** verified — that must be done on a server with the correct key.
Encrypted JWE tokens (5 parts) cannot be read.

pairs.q: "A JWT must have 3 parts"
pairs.a: Copy the full token (header.payload.signature). A `Bearer ` prefix is removed automatically.

pairs.q: Base64 decoded to binary data.
pairs.a: The content is not UTF-8 text (maybe an image or file). This tool only displays text.

pairs.q: "Web Crypto is not available"
pairs.a: Open the page over HTTPS so Hash Generator works.

pairs.q: A function/expression cannot be converted to JSON.
pairs.a: Replace that value with a literal; only data is supported.

media.title: Media tools
media.summary: Image, video, and audio tools that run right in your browser: fast, private, and files never leave your device.

sections.heading: Tool list
items: **Images**: Image Converter, Find Colors at Image, Remove Background, Image Upscaler, Remove Image Metadata, Favicon Generator, OG Image Maker.
**Video & audio**: Video to Frames, Extract Audio, Audio Converter.
Every tool runs in the browser; files are never uploaded.

sections.heading: How to use it
items: Open **All Media tools** for an overview, or pick a tool from the sidebar.
Drop files on the upload area, set options, then run and download the results.

sections.heading: Input & output formats
items: Image Converter: input PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP, ICO, AVIF, SVG; output PNG, JPEG, WebP, or SVG (tracing). GIF/BMP/ICO/AVIF cannot be re-encoded and are saved as PNG.
Remove Background: transparent PNG output. Remove Image Metadata: lossless for JPEG/PNG/WebP; GIF/BMP/AVIF are re-encoded to PNG.
Extract Audio: the output is WAV.
Video to Frames: browser mode only handles browser-supported codecs (usually H.264/MP4, WebM).

sections.heading: Browser-mode limits
items: Image Converter max. 100 MB per file, 200 files, ±50 megapixels. Find Colors max. 60 MB. Remove Image Metadata max. 50 MB per file.
Remove Background max. 20 MB per file; first use downloads an AI model of about 115 MB (Light) or 224 MB (Precise).
Image Upscaler: output max. 16.7 megapixels; sharpens edges, not AI reconstruction.
Video to Frames max. 300 MB and 600 frames. Extract Audio max. 200 MB video and 20 minutes of audio.

pairs.q: A video fails in the browser.
pairs.a: Codecs such as HEVC/H.265 or ProRes are often unsupported by browsers. Convert to MP4 H.264 first.

pairs.q: Remove Background is slow.
pairs.a: The AI model runs on your device; phones and older devices can take tens of seconds per image.

page-maker.title: Page Designer (Page Maker)
page-maker.summary: A visual editor for designing one page from sections, Rows, and elements, then exporting its code to HTML, React, Vue, Svelte, or Angular.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.body: One Page Maker design = one page. Designs can be grouped into a website in the **Website** menu.

sections.heading: How to use it
items: Page structure: **section** → **Row** → elements. Create a section from the preset picker first, then add Rows and elements.
Drag element cards onto the canvas or the **Structure** panel, or click **+**. Adjust the look in Settings.
Switch between **Design**, **Preview**, and **Code** modes; check Desktop, Tablet (768px), and Mobile (375px).
Save and open designs via **My Page Designs**. Undo with Ctrl+Z.

sections.heading: Code export
items: **Code** mode offers HTML, React, Vue, Svelte, and Angular. A single file downloads directly; several files download as a ZIP.
JavaScript events are written as the handler body (an `event` variable is available) and are included in exports; they run in Preview mode, not on the design canvas.

sections.heading: Limits
items: **Unlimited** saved page designs. The app **never** deletes designs automatically.
**Unlimited** code exports, generated right in the browser.
All **32** section presets are ready to use.
Every element is available, including Product Card, Slider, Countdown, Progress Bar, Testimoni (testimonial), and Kartu Harga (pricing card).
Every event is available: onClick, onChange, onInput, onKeyDown, and more.

pairs.q: "Create a section before adding elements."
pairs.a: Elements live inside Rows, and Rows inside sections. Add a section from the preset picker.

pairs.q: Event code is missing from the output.
pairs.a: Check its syntax; invalid code is ignored.

website.title: Build Full Website
website.summary: Group Page Maker designs into website folders: set the homepage, page addresses, and menu order, then preview and export the whole site.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.body: A website folder stores **references** to designs, not copies. Renamed designs update the menu automatically, and removing a page from a folder does not delete its design.

sections.heading: How to use it
items: Type a name and press **Create folder**, or **Start from a template**.
Add designs from the saved designs list with **Add to folder**.
Reorder pages (order = menu order), fill in the menu label and slug, then choose **Set as homepage**.
Open the **Preview** tab to try navigation, or **Website code** to export.

**SEO & sharing (v10)**: enter the site URL, description, and share image in the SEO panel. Each page can have its own title and description. Exports automatically include SEO meta, Open Graph, robots.txt, and sitemap.xml (the sitemap needs the site URL).

sections.heading: Export output
sections.body: One export = the whole website in one ZIP for the chosen framework, including routing and a README.
items: HTML: `index.html` (homepage) + `<slug>.html`, CSS/JS in `assets/`.
React (`react-router-dom`), Vue (`vue-router`), Svelte (built-in hash routing), Angular (`@angular/router`).

sections.heading: Limits
items: **Unlimited** website folders.
Max. **50** pages per website.
Slug: lowercase a–z, digits, and hyphens, max. 60 characters, unique per website; `index`, `assets`, `src`, `app`, `pages` are not allowed.

pairs.q: A page is skipped in preview/export.
pairs.a: Its source design was deleted. Use **Replace…** to pick another design, or remove the page.

pairs.q: A slug is rejected.
pairs.a: Use only lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, and make sure no other page uses it.

templates.title: Website Templates
templates.summary: **400** responsive website templates built from Page Maker elements: preview, download the source code, or open one as a new website to edit.

sections.heading: Available templates
items: **400** ready-made templates across many categories: company profile, landing page, online shop, portfolio, and more.
Filter by category or search by name.

sections.heading: How to use it
items: Filter by category, then press **Preview** to try a template; click the menu inside the preview to switch pages.
**Download source**: downloads a ready-to-use ZIP.
**Use this template**: creates a new website folder with one design per page, then opens Studio. The original template is unchanged.
If you have used the template before, a dialog offers to **Open** the existing website or create a new copy.

sections.heading: Download contents
items: Static HTML + CSS, SVG images in `assets/img/`, and a `README.md` with instructions.
Open `index.html` in a browser or upload the folder to static hosting.

sections.heading: Notes
items: Every template can be previewed, downloaded, and edited.
Editing creates a new website folder with one design per page; the original template stays unchanged.
Text, prices, contacts, and products are samples. Forms and shopping buttons do not process payments.

pairs.q: Download preparation failed.
pairs.a: Try again; the download is built in the browser and saved to your browser's download location.

global-setting.title: Global Settings
global-setting.summary: Shared icon and font libraries for Page Maker and web templates, stored in this browser.

sections.heading: What it does
items: **Icons**: an SVG icon library offered as choices in Button, Card, Badge, and other elements.
**Fonts**: a font library from Google Fonts or a URL, plus the **Page base font** for Page Maker and its exported code.

sections.heading: How to use it
items: **Icons** tab: **Upload .svg** or **Paste SVG code**, name it, then **Save icon**. Icons can be renamed or deleted.
**Fonts** tab: choose Google Fonts (type the name exactly as on fonts.google.com) or a URL, pick a fallback and weights, then **Add to library**.
Font status shows **Loaded** or **Failed to load**.

sections.heading: Input & output formats
items: Icons: SVG code starting with `<svg>` and ending with `</svg>`; SVG is sanitized before display.
Font URL: a `.woff2`, `.woff`, `.ttf`, `.otf` file or a CSS stylesheet; must be `https://` or a site-root path.

sections.heading: Limits
items: Icons max. **200 KB** per file.
Font name: letters, digits, spaces, `-` and `_`, max. 60 characters; no duplicates.
Data is stored in this browser only; it is not synced to other devices.

pairs.q: "The pasted code is not valid SVG"
pairs.a: Make sure the code is complete from `<svg` to `</svg>`.

pairs.q: Font "Failed to load".
pairs.a: Check the Google Font name spelling or the URL (must be https), then try again.

pairs.q: Deleting an icon or font.
pairs.a: Elements using that icon end up without an icon; elements using that font fall back to the fallback font.

vr.title: 360° Tour (VR)
vr.summary: Build a virtual tour from 360° panorama photos: move between rooms with hotspots, add info, images and audio, then download it as an HTML site that runs in browsers and VR headsets.

sections.heading: Purpose
items: A **tour** holds several **scenes** (one panorama photo each).
**Hotspots** are placed directly on the panorama: *Go to scene*, *Info* (text), *Image* or *Audio*.
The export uses **A-Frame 1.6.0** from the jsDelivr CDN. Its link is added to the `<head>` of index.html automatically.

sections.heading: How to use
items: Open **VR → 360° Tour**, name the tour, then **Create tour**.
Pick a scene and upload a panorama photo (drag onto the upload box or click).
In **Place hotspots** mode, choose a hotspot type and click a spot on the panorama. Set its label, target scene, text or file in the right panel.
Use **Try the tour** mode to test it like a visitor.
Click **Download tour (.zip)**. Upload the zip contents to hosting, or run a local server (see README.md inside the zip).

sections.heading: Input & output formats
items: Panorama: equirectangular JPG, PNG or WebP with a **2:1** ratio (e.g. 6000×3000), max **25 MB**.
Hotspot image: JPG/PNG/WebP up to 8 MB. Hotspot audio: MP3/WAV/OGG up to 10 MB.
File types are checked from their content, not the file name.
Output: `index.html`, `README.md` and an `assets/` folder with photos & audio.

sections.heading: Limits
items: **Unlimited** tours, scenes per tour, and hotspots per scene.
Every hotspot type: *Go to scene*, *Info*, *Image*, and *Audio*.
Tours and their files are stored in this browser (IndexedDB).

pairs.q: Panorama is black after opening the zip.
pairs.a: The file was opened by double-clicking (file://). Open it through a web server; see README.md.

pairs.q: Panorama looks squashed or warped.
pairs.a: The photo is not a 2:1 equirectangular image. Use your camera/app's 360° panorama mode.

pairs.q: Preview does not show.
pairs.a: The preview needs access to the jsDelivr CDN and a browser with WebGL.

pairs.q: Info panels don't show in a headset.
pairs.a: In VR mode, scene hotspots work with gaze/laser; info, image and audio panels show in normal screen mode.

data-pdf.title: PDF Tools
data-pdf.summary: 9 PDF tools that run in your browser: merge, split, compress, PDF to image, image to PDF, and extract/delete/rotate/reorder pages. Files are never uploaded.

sections.heading: Tools
items: **Merge PDF**, **Split PDF** (per page, every N pages, or by range), **Compress PDF**.
**PDF to Image** (JPG/PNG/WebP, 72–300 DPI) and **Image to PDF** (A4, Letter, or original size).
**Extract**, **Delete**, **Rotate**, and **Reorder** pages.

sections.heading: How to use
items: Choose a tool and a PDF, set the options, then press the action button. The result downloads right away.
Write page ranges like `1-3, 5, 8-`. `8-` means page 8 to the end. Leave empty for all pages (Rotate, PDF to Image).
Multi-file results (Split, PDF to Image) download as a ZIP.

sections.heading: Limits
items: No uploads. Max 200 MB per PDF, 50 PDFs to merge, 200 images per PDF.
**Light/Medium/Strong** compression turns pages into images: much smaller, but text can no longer be selected or searched. Use **Keep content** when text must stay copyable.
Password-protected PDFs must be unlocked first.

pairs.q: "This PDF is password-protected"
pairs.a: Open it in a PDF reader, save it without a password, and try again.

pairs.q: The compressed file is not smaller
pairs.a: Text-only PDFs are usually small already. Light–Strong work best for scanned or photo-heavy PDFs.
